title: Rust Language Indexing Support
description: Roadmap for making Rust language indexing useful beyond structural TS-indexed fallback.

decisions.q: How do we avoid losing explore/exploit work while starting Rust indexing?
decisions.answer: Track all known explore and exploit branches in the roadmap now. Start implementation with bounded Rust core ownership for .rs files, while keeping module paths, traits, macros, Cargo workspace/features, framework routes, validation, and product surface as explicit nodes.
decisions.note: This prevents the first implementation slice from silently redefining full Rust language support.

decisions.q: After the first six Rust language indexing slices, should we expand the global roadmap or continue directly to slice 7?
decisions.answer: Expand and reconcile the global roadmap first before starting slice 7.
decisions.note: The first six slices completed the current Rust semantic graph slice subtree, but stale pending taxonomy nodes still exist under 1-1-3. Reconcile covered taxonomy, bounded solutions, and remaining frontier before choosing the next implementation slice.

1-1.label: Rust language support baseline and taxonomy

decisions.q: What is the current Rust language indexing boundary?
decisions.answer: Current .rs support is Rust-owned baseline structural indexing through rust-hybrid. Full Rust semantic graph work remains explicitly tracked under 1-4.
decisions.note: This supersedes the initial pre-Plan-1 audit where .rs still used the mature TypeScript indexer path.

decisions.q: What is the current Rust language indexing boundary after Plan 1?
decisions.answer: Current .rs support is Rust-owned baseline structural indexing through rust-hybrid. Full Rust semantic graph work remains explicitly tracked under 1-4.

1-1.notes: Initial baseline/taxonomy discussion superseded by Plan 1 implementation; remaining semantic gaps are tracked under 1-4.

decisions.q: Should the first implementation slice make Rust core own .rs baseline extraction?
decisions.answer: Yes. First add bounded Rust core .rs baseline extraction and rust-hybrid ownership; do not include trait coherence, macro expansion, Cargo feature resolution, or compiler-grade semantics in this slice.
decisions.note: This creates the foundation for later Rust semantic graph slices without pretending the first slice completes full Rust language intelligence.

decisions.q: What is included in the first Rust language indexing implementation slice?
decisions.answer: Accept bounded baseline extraction: Rust core owns .rs files for basic structure, imports, and calls. Exclude trait dispatch, macro expansion, Cargo feature resolution, and compiler-grade Rust semantics.
decisions.note: Those deeper semantics remain tracked under 1-4 Rust semantic graph slices.

decisions.q: Which GitHub issues implement Rust core .rs ownership Plan 1?
decisions.answer: #566 covers parser ownership; #567 covers baseline .rs graph extraction; #568 covers rust-hybrid .rs assignment and diagnostics; #569 covers validation, guardrails, and evidence.
decisions.note: Published with enhancement + ready-for-agent labels in dependency order.

decisions.q: What changed in Plan 1?
decisions.answer: Rust core now owns .rs baseline parsing/extraction and rust-hybrid includes rust in Rust-owned languages. Deeper Rust semantic graph work remains under 1-4.

1-4-1.label: Rust repo-local module path resolution slice

decisions.q: What is Plan 2's target slice?
decisions.answer: Implement Rust repo-local module path resolution for crate/self/super/mod/sibling module paths, bounded to local files and symbols. Exclude Cargo package/dependency resolution, feature cfg, macro expansion, and trait dispatch.

decisions.q: What graph edge boundary should Plan 2 use?
decisions.answer: Prefer file-level dependency edges for Rust repo-local module paths. Add symbol-level references/calls only when the target symbol is high-confidence and unique; otherwise record taxonomy rather than guessing.

decisions.q: Which Rust path forms are in Plan 2?
decisions.answer: Support repo-local module basics: mod/pub mod declarations, crate/self/super use paths, sibling qualified call/type refs, foo.rs and foo/mod.rs targets, and src/lib.rs or src/main.rs crate roots. Defer pub use re-export chains, glob imports, alias imports, external crates, #[path] modules, and cfg-specific variants.

decisions.q: Which corpus validates Plan 2?
decisions.answer: Use mini-redis as the primary real Rust repository smoke, with compact synthetic fixtures for exact boundary tests. Defer larger Rust corpora such as ripgrep or hyper until module path semantics are stable.

decisions.q: What validation gate completes Plan 2?
decisions.answer: Require deterministic graph tests plus a mini-redis smoke and deterministic explore probe. Do not run stochastic agent A/B. Evidence must include graph counts, fallback/deferred taxonomy, status/doctor/profile signal, and RSS or unavailable reason.

decisions.q: Where should Plan 2 implementation live?
decisions.answer: Keep Rust repo-local module resolution Rust-owned: collect module identities, mod declarations, use paths, and qualified refs in Rust core, then resolve/write file-level edges and taxonomy inside Rust-owned extraction/finalization. Do not route .rs same-language semantics back through the TypeScript resolver.

decisions.q: How should Plan 2 be split into issues?
decisions.answer: Split into 4 issues: module identity/mod declaration target mapping; crate/self/super use path file-level dependencies; sibling qualified refs with file-level plus unique symbol edges; mini-redis smoke, deterministic explore probe, and evidence/status taxonomy.

1-4-1.notes: Plan 2 repo-local module path resolution slice completed.

1-4-2.label: Rust trait definition to impl relationship frontier

decisions.q: What is the third Rust semantic graph slice?
decisions.answer: Prioritize Rust trait definition to impl relationship frontier before macro, Cargo workspace, or web framework route slices.
decisions.note: Chosen because repo-local module paths are now connected, and trait/impl structure is the next highest-leverage Rust sufficiency gap.

decisions.q: Should Plan 3 be taxonomy-only or include implementation?
decisions.answer: Use taxonomy plus one bounded exploit slice: record Rust trait/impl forms and write only high-confidence structural edges. Do not implement dynamic trait dispatch, generic bound resolution, blanket impls, where-clause exactness, macro-expanded impls, or cross-crate trait resolution.
decisions.note: This keeps Plan 3 useful without pretending to solve full Rust trait semantics.

decisions.q: Which graph edge kinds should Rust trait/impl use?
decisions.answer: Reuse existing edge kinds:  for Type -> Trait, existing  for trait/method containment, and bounded  from impl method to trait method declaration when the match is unique. Do not add new EdgeKind values in this slice.
decisions.note: Avoids public schema expansion while still giving agents structural Rust trait/impl context.

decisions.q: Correction: which graph edge kinds should Rust trait/impl use?
decisions.answer: Reuse existing edge kinds: implements for Type -> Trait, contains for trait/method containment, and bounded references from impl method to trait method declaration when the match is unique. Do not add new EdgeKind values in this slice.
decisions.note: Corrects the previous shell-escaped decision text where edge kind names were accidentally stripped.

decisions.q: What validation corpus should Plan 3 use?
decisions.answer: Use deterministic synthetic fixtures for exact trait/impl graph behavior, and mini-redis as the real repo smoke. If mini-redis has limited trait/impl coverage, record that honestly instead of switching corpora mid-slice.
decisions.note: Keeps behavior verification precise while still guarding the real Rust repo path.

decisions.q: How should Plan 3 be split into issues?
decisions.answer: Split into 4 issues: trait/impl extraction taxonomy; Type implements Trait structural edge; impl method to trait method declaration bounded references; mini-redis smoke, evidence, and roadmap closeout.
decisions.note: Keeps implementation vertical and avoids mixing taxonomy, structural edges, and evidence in one issue.

decisions.q: What is the fifth Rust semantic graph slice?
decisions.answer: Prioritize Rust macro coverage taxonomy frontier before Rust web framework route wiring candidates.
decisions.note: Chosen because Rust route wiring often depends on macro and attribute forms; taxonomy first prevents later route slices from guessing unsupported macro-expanded semantics.

decisions.q: Should Plan 5 be taxonomy-only or include bounded implementation?
decisions.answer: Use taxonomy plus bounded extraction guardrail. Record Rust macro taxonomy and explicitly classify supported/deferred macro-related forms without expanding macros or guessing semantic edges.
decisions.note: macro_rules! definitions, function-like macro invocations, derive attributes, attribute macros, cfg_attr, proc macros, and macro-generated impl/route shapes should become visible taxonomy. The extractor must fail closed around macro-expanded semantics.

decisions.q: Should Plan 5 write graph nodes or edges?
decisions.answer: Do not write new graph nodes or edges in Plan 5. Write profile taxonomy and diagnostics only.
decisions.note: Avoid adding a macro NodeKind or guessed macro invocation edges. Macro resolution and expansion are too broad for this slice; diagnostics-only keeps later route wiring honest.

decisions.q: What is the minimum macro taxonomy coverage set for Plan 5?
decisions.answer: Cover six core macro-related shapes: macro_rules! definitions; function-like macro invocations; derive attributes; attribute macros; cfg/cfg_attr attributes; macro-affected semantic regions around impl/trait/mod/route-like functions as deferred taxonomy.
decisions.note: This is enough to support later Rust web framework route wiring without entering compiler-grade macro expansion.

decisions.q: What validation corpus should Plan 5 use?
decisions.answer: Use a deterministic synthetic macro fixture, mini-redis smoke, and one optional reasonably sized macro-rich Rust repo if local setup is available.
decisions.note: The third repo should not block the mainline. Prefer a macro-focused or broadly used repo such as dtolnay/async-trait or BurntSushi/ripgrep over a heavy route-framework repo, so Plan 5 stays macro taxonomy rather than route wiring.

decisions.q: How should Plan 5 be split into issues?
decisions.answer: Split into 4 issues: Rust macro syntax taxonomy extraction; macro-affected semantic region guardrail; profile/result JSON diagnostics surface; synthetic plus mini-redis plus optional macro-rich repo evidence and closeout.
decisions.note: This keeps syntax taxonomy, fail-closed semantic guardrails, diagnostics surface, and evidence separate without making optional corpus setup a blocker.

decisions.q: Should Plan 5 be written as a repository plan document now?
decisions.answer: Write a narrow repository plan document for Plan 5 before publishing issues.
decisions.note: Macro semantics are slippery; the plan must pin non-goals including no macro expansion, no macro graph nodes or edges, no new NodeKind, and no route wiring.

1-4-4.label: Cargo workspace package and feature taxonomy frontier

decisions.q: What is the fourth Rust semantic graph slice?
decisions.answer: Prioritize Cargo workspace package and feature taxonomy frontier before macro coverage or Rust web framework route wiring.
decisions.note: Chosen because repo-local modules and trait/impl structure are now connected, and real Rust projects need package/workspace boundaries before framework route wiring can be reliable.

decisions.q: Should Plan 4 be taxonomy-only or include bounded implementation?
decisions.answer: Use taxonomy plus bounded package/workspace discovery. Parse Cargo.toml package metadata, lib/bin roots, workspace members, and local path dependencies; classify workspace-local crate candidates without attempting a full Cargo resolver.
decisions.note: Do not implement feature resolution, cfg target selection, build.rs, proc macros, registry dependency resolution, semver dependency graph, or target-specific dependency exactness.

decisions.q: Should Plan 4 write graph edges?
decisions.answer: Do not write cross-package graph edges in Plan 4. Produce package/workspace diagnostics and bounded taxonomy only: file ownership, crate roots, workspace-local candidates, external dependency candidates, unresolved candidates, and deferred feature/cfg/build.rs/proc-macro cases.
decisions.note: This avoids false cross-crate edges before feature/cfg and full Cargo resolution are designed.

decisions.q: What validation corpus should Plan 4 use?
decisions.answer: Use a synthetic Cargo workspace fixture plus mini-redis smoke. If the fixture is insufficient, add one reasonably sized real GitHub Rust workspace repo as optional validation, but do not let external corpus setup block the Plan 4 mainline.
decisions.note: mini-redis remains the stable no-regression smoke; the synthetic fixture covers workspace members and local path dependencies deterministically.

decisions.q: Plan 4 should be split into how many implementation issues?
decisions.answer: Split into 4 issues: Cargo.toml package/workspace metadata taxonomy; Rust file package/crate-root ownership diagnostics; workspace-local crate candidate taxonomy for use crate_name::...; synthetic workspace + mini-redis smoke + optional real repo evidence + closeout.
decisions.note: This keeps optional real-repo validation non-blocking while preserving clear diagnostic boundaries.

decisions.q: Where should the Plan 4 artifact live?
decisions.answer: Write a narrow repository plan document and keep the roadmap updated.
decisions.note: Use a dedicated plan document because this slice has explicit non-goals and must not drift into full Cargo resolver implementation.

1-4-5.label: Rust web framework route wiring candidates

decisions.q: What is the sixth Rust semantic graph slice?
decisions.answer: Enter 1-4-5. Rust web framework route wiring candidates, bounded to route candidate taxonomy plus one safe framework slice.
decisions.note: Prior module, trait, macro, and Cargo workspace slices provide enough guardrails. Do not implement all Rust web frameworks at once.

decisions.q: Which Rust web framework route shape should Plan 6 target first?
decisions.answer: Axum explicit router call slice: classify and resolve Router::new().route(path, get/post/put/delete(handler)) to a handler candidate when local and unambiguous.
decisions.note: This gives a concrete route wiring slice without requiring macro expansion, middleware semantics, nesting semantics, state/extractor modeling, or package-wide framework support.

decisions.q: Should Plan 6 write route graph edges or only taxonomy?
decisions.answer: Write guarded route nodes plus references edges only for static Axum paths and repo-local unique handler candidates; otherwise record taxonomy/deferred reasons.
decisions.note: This makes the slice useful for agent sufficiency while preserving correctness. No nesting, middleware, fallback, state, extractor, macro, or multi-candidate inference.

decisions.q: What validation corpus should Plan 6 require?
decisions.answer: Use synthetic Axum fixture plus mini-redis smoke; treat a real Axum repository as optional evidence, not a blocking requirement.
decisions.note: The fixture locks the route syntax and guarded edge contract deterministically; mini-redis preserves the existing Rust smoke guardrail without adding setup risk.

decisions.q: How should Plan 6 be split into issues?
decisions.answer: Split into 4 issues: Axum route syntax taxonomy; static path plus local handler candidate resolution; guarded route node/reference edge write plus deferred reasons; synthetic Axum fixture plus mini-redis smoke plus closeout evidence.
decisions.note: This keeps recognition, candidate resolution, graph writing, and validation independently reviewable while avoiding optional real Axum corpus setup as a blocker.

decisions.q: Which GitHub issues track Plan 6?
decisions.answer: Published #586, #587, #588, and #589 in dependency order with enhancement + ready-for-agent labels.
decisions.note: Issues map to taxonomy, candidate resolution, guarded graph write, and validation/closeout evidence.

decisions.q: What is the Plan 6 closeout result?
decisions.answer: Completed bounded Axum explicit route wiring: taxonomy, unique handler candidate resolution, guarded route-to-handler edges, result JSON diagnostics, and mini-redis smoke evidence.
decisions.note: Evidence: docs/benchmarks/2026-06-27-rust-language-indexing-plan-6-axum-route-wiring-evidence.md. Remaining Axum nesting, middleware, fallback, state/extractor, macro routes, and other Rust frameworks stay out of scope.

1-5.label: Rust language semantic frontier after Plan 6

decisions.q: How should the post-Plan-6 Rust semantic frontier be classified?
decisions.answer: Classify the first layer by semantic ownership frontier: module/visibility, trait/generic dispatch, macro/cfg/generated code, Cargo/package/feature conditional semantics, and framework route/runtime semantics beyond bounded Axum.
decisions.note: Readiness should be tracked inside each frontier node as mode/status, not as the top-level taxonomy. This restores global map shape before choosing slice 7.

decisions.q: Which post-Plan-6 frontier should slice 7 start from?
decisions.answer: Start with 1-5-1 Module path visibility and privacy residuals as an explore slice.
decisions.note: Module and visibility semantics are foundational for later trait, macro, Cargo cfg, and framework route work; first map the residual boundary before writing another implementation slice.

decisions.q: Which post-visibility semantic frontier should slice 8 start from?
decisions.answer: Start with 1-5-2 Trait generic and dispatch residuals.
decisions.note: Module visibility wrong-edge guard is complete. Trait/generic dispatch is now the highest-leverage correctness frontier because existing bounded trait edges can become wrong or insufficient around generics, blanket impls, where clauses, cross-crate traits, dyn dispatch, and method ambiguity.

decisions.q: Which semantic frontier should slice 9 start from?
decisions.answer: Start with 1-5-3 Macro cfg and generated-code frontier.
decisions.note: Trait/generic dispatch residuals are classified. Macro/cfg generated-code semantics now need a frontier map because they can invalidate visibility, trait, cargo feature, and framework route assumptions.

1-5-1.label: Module path visibility and privacy residuals

decisions.q: What should the module visibility residual slice deliver?
decisions.answer: Deliver explore-only residual taxonomy, readiness ranking, and one recommended bounded implementation candidate for the next slice; do not implement visibility enforcement yet.
decisions.note: Visibility and privacy can either improve correct resolution or prevent wrong edges. Separate the semantic boundary before writing new production behavior.

decisions.q: How should module visibility residual taxonomy be organized?
decisions.answer: Organize by resolution correctness impact: missing-edge residuals, wrong-edge risk residuals, ambiguity residuals, and no-go/oracle-needed residuals.
decisions.note: This keeps the taxonomy tied to graph correctness decisions instead of a syntax inventory, making the next bounded implementation candidate easier to select.

decisions.q: Should the module visibility residual explore slice write an evidence or decision artifact?
decisions.answer: Write a narrow decision artifact in docs/benchmarks as the slice deliverable.
decisions.note: This is the first slice after global roadmap reconciliation. A durable artifact should preserve the taxonomy basis, readiness ranking, recommended next candidate, and non-goals for the next agent.

decisions.q: Which bounded implementation candidate should the module visibility decision artifact recommend?
decisions.answer: Recommend wrong-edge guard for private or out-of-scope module symbols before missing-edge expansion.
decisions.note: After six coverage-expanding slices, the next risk is overconfident wrong edges. A bounded visibility guard makes later expansion safer than immediately adding more path shapes.

decisions.q: Should the decision artifact be based on a current code audit?
decisions.answer: Do a lightweight code-fact audit before writing the artifact.
decisions.note: Audit only the current Rust module resolver, edge write guards, and symbol visibility extraction. Do not run a new large corpus, implement behavior, create issues, or add a rustc/cargo metadata oracle.

decisions.q: What did the module visibility residual explore artifact conclude?
decisions.answer: Recommend the next bounded implementation as a Rust module visibility wrong-edge guard for private or out-of-scope symbols.
decisions.note: Artifact: docs/benchmarks/2026-06-27-rust-module-visibility-residual-taxonomy-decision.md. Code audit found module/scoped resolution writes unique symbol edges without visibility guard, while nodes.visibility is currently persisted as NULL by Rust core.

1-5-1.notes: Slice 7 candidate: explore module path visibility and privacy residuals before choosing bounded implementation work.

1-5-2.label: Trait generic and dispatch residuals

decisions.q: What should slice 8 deliver?
decisions.answer: Explore-only residual taxonomy, readiness ranking, and one recommended bounded implementation candidate.
decisions.note: Do not implement trait dispatch behavior in this slice. The purpose is to map correctness risk before writing more semantic edges.

decisions.q: How should trait/generic dispatch residual taxonomy be organized?
decisions.answer: Organize by edge-write correctness risk.
decisions.note: Buckets: safe-ish exploit candidates, needs-guard candidates, needs-oracle/research, and defer/no-go taxonomy. This keeps later work focused on avoiding wrong semantic edges.

decisions.q: Which trait/generic residuals should slice 8 audit?
decisions.answer: Audit the trait/impl extraction and finalization boundaries Rust core already touches.
decisions.note: Include inherent-vs-trait impl stability, impl Trait for Type uniqueness, impl method to trait method declaration references, generic/blanket/where taxonomy, cross-crate trait no-go status, dyn dispatch needs-oracle status, associated type/generic bound needs-oracle status, and same-file versus cross-file relationship readiness.

decisions.q: Should slice 8 run a real repo smoke?
decisions.answer: Yes, run a mini-redis deterministic taxonomy smoke only.
decisions.note: Use it to summarize trait impl taxonomy and existing trait-related graph edges. Do not run agent A/B, performance gates, or additional implementation in this explore slice.

decisions.q: Where should slice 8 write its artifact?
decisions.answer: Write a decision/evidence artifact under docs/benchmarks and record the closeout decision in the roadmap.
decisions.note: Planned artifact: docs/benchmarks/2026-06-27-rust-trait-generic-dispatch-residual-taxonomy-decision.md. Do not create a PRD or implementation plan from this explore slice.

decisions.q: What bounded implementation candidate should slice 8 recommend next?
decisions.answer: Recommend Rust trait impl edge guard v1 plus taxonomy hardening.
decisions.note: Do not expand into dyn dispatch or generic inference. The next bounded implementation should make existing Type implements Trait and impl-method to trait-method writes fail closed for generic, blanket, where-clause, cross-crate, or ambiguous cases unless a low-risk unique repo-local candidate is proven.

decisions.q: What is the slice 8 closeout decision?
decisions.answer: Complete: trait generic and dispatch residuals are classified; next step should harden existing trait impl edge writes before expanding dispatch coverage.
decisions.note: Artifact: docs/benchmarks/2026-06-27-rust-trait-generic-dispatch-residual-taxonomy-decision.md. mini-redis smoke shows trait/impl taxonomy exists, but no trait semantic edges are written there yet; this supports guard-hardening before missing-edge expansion.

1-5-2.notes: Completed as explore-only slice 8. Decision artifact: docs/benchmarks/2026-06-27-rust-trait-generic-dispatch-residual-taxonomy-decision.md. Recommended next candidate: Rust trait impl edge guard v1 plus taxonomy hardening.

1-5-3.label: Macro cfg and generated-code frontier

decisions.q: What should slice 9 deliver?
decisions.answer: Explore-only macro/cfg/generated-code frontier taxonomy, readiness ranking, and one recommended bounded implementation candidate.
decisions.note: Do not implement cfg-aware filtering, macro expansion, or generated symbol recovery in this slice. The goal is to prevent future implementation from writing optimistic wrong edges around generated or conditionally compiled Rust code.

decisions.q: How should macro/cfg frontier taxonomy be organized?
decisions.answer: Organize by code existence and semantic generation mode.
decisions.note: Buckets: always-present parsed AST, conditionally-present AST, macro-affected parsed item, macro-generated missing item, macro invocation opaque region, and external build/generated code. This better predicts graph correctness risk than syntax-only classification.

decisions.q: Which macro/cfg scenarios should slice 9 audit?
decisions.answer: Audit only macro/cfg scenarios Rust core already exposes or depends on.
decisions.note: Include item-level cfg/cfg_attr, derive/proc macro attributes, macro-affected impl/trait/mod/route-like functions, function-like macro invocation, macro_rules definitions/invocations, include/build generated code taxonomy, Axum route macro interactions, and the relationship between cfg-impl-deferred and macro taxonomy.

decisions.q: Should slice 9 run a real repo smoke?
decisions.answer: Yes, run a mini-redis deterministic macro/cfg taxonomy smoke only.
decisions.note: Record rustMacroTaxonomyCounts, cfg-impl-deferred, route taxonomy interaction, and whether graph writes remain conservative around macro-generated semantics. Do not run agent A/B or performance gates.

decisions.q: Where should slice 9 write its artifact?
decisions.answer: Write a decision/evidence artifact under docs/benchmarks and record closeout in the roadmap.
decisions.note: Planned artifact: docs/benchmarks/2026-06-27-rust-macro-cfg-generated-code-frontier-decision.md. Do not create an implementation plan from this explore slice.

decisions.q: What bounded implementation candidate should slice 9 recommend next?
decisions.answer: Recommend Macro/cfg diagnostic hardening v1.

decisions.q: What should slice 7 implement?
decisions.answer: Implement Rust module visibility wrong-edge guard v1: coarse visibility extraction plus cross-module scoped symbol edge guard.
decisions.note: Scope is repo-local same-crate Rust module files. Persist coarse visibility for Rust symbols and fail closed before writing cross-module scoped symbol edges when visibility is private, unknown, or unsupported. Do not implement pub use expansion, external crate semantics, macro/cfg semantics, or full rustc privacy.

decisions.q: What is the default behavior for Rust visibility guarded scoped symbol edges?
decisions.answer: Fail closed: cross-file scoped symbol edges are written only when coarse visibility allows them; private, unknown, and unsupported visibility skip edge write and record taxonomy.
decisions.note: Same-file edges are unaffected. Cross-file pub and same-crate pub(crate) may write. Conservative pub(super) can write only for a supported parent/descendant relationship. pub(in ...) and unknown visibility are deferred. Skipped refs remain unresolved.

decisions.q: How should slice 7 be split into implementation issues?
